newsitem.title: UK: Iranian demand prevails on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Iranian demand prevails on sugar freight market.

text.p: Iranian demand dominated new inquiry on the sugar freight market on Tuesday but firmer business was thin on the ground, shipbrokers said.
Iranian shippers IRISL quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from the U.K. to Iran for 15 February/15 March, they said.

Universal was open for 14,000 tonnes, also in bags, from Thailand to Iran for 1/10 February and Seven Seas quoted for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Antwerp-Hamburg range to Dubai for prompt dates.
Tate & Lyle was in the market for 10,400/10,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to the Finnish port of Porkkala for 15/20 February.
Other orders included Cargill with 8,500 tonnes from Thailand to Japan for early March and Louis Dreyfus with 6,000 tonnes from the same origin to Colombo for early February.
Of the day's firmer business, shipbrokers said CSR fixed 17,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for January loading at a little over $21.

Kerry Trading was said to have fixed a 14,000-tonne bulk cargo from Thailand to South Korea for 1/10 February and Dreyfus was closely working 14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia fpr January/February dates.
E D & F Man was still seeking tonnage to ship a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Mexico to Colombo, and the recent order from Louis Dreyfus for 1,000 tonnes in bags from Odessa to Poti.
Shipbrokers said they were closely monitoring the situation in Colombia, where a six-day strike at the Pacific port of Buenaventura has paralysed sugar exports.
Physical market sources said South Korea could have bought up to five cargoes of raw sugar from Thailand for delivery in March or April.
